A 24-year-old G2P2002 woman is hospitalized on postpartum day 3 following a low transverse
cesarean delivery. During morning rounds, she reports experiencing shaking chills overnight and
noticing a “pus-like” discharge. She also mentions increased uterine cramping compared to the
previous day. Her postpartum recovery has otherwise been uneventful, with a well-healing incision and

normal vaginal bleeding. Her prenatal history includes HIV with a recent viral load of 400 copies/mL,
well-controlled type I diabetes managed with insulin, and a history of neonatal herpes simplex virus
encephalitis in her first child. She had no genital lesions during her most recent pregnancy. Four days
prior, she presented with spontaneous rupture of membranes and labor onset. After 16 hours of slow
cervical progression and arrest of descent due to cephalopelvic disproportion, a cesarean delivery was
performed with prophylactic ampicillin. Delivery required manual dislodgment of the fetal head. On
postpartum day 3, her temperature is 102.5°F (38.6°C), blood pressure is 113/68 mmHg, pulse is
60/min, and respirations are 18/min. Examination reveals a clean, dry incision, mild suprapubic
tenderness, and foul-smelling, blood-tinged yellow discharge on her pad. Which of the following
represents the most significant risk factor for her current condition? Answer Choices: (A) Well-healing
surgical incision (B) Suboptimal viral load control in pregnancy (C) C-section after onset of labor (D)
Prolonged labor lasting >16 hours (E) Vaginal hand manipulation during delivery (F) HIV infection
during pregnancy (G) History of herpes simplex virus encephalitis in prior child (H) Prolonged rupture of
membranes (I) History of type I diabetes mellitus (J) HIV positive status
 A. History of herpes simplex virus encephalitis in prior child
B. Well-healing surgical incision
C. C-section after onset of labor
D. HIV positive status
E. Vaginal hand manipulation during delivery
F. HIV infection during pregnancy
G. Suboptimal viral load control in pregnancy
H. Prolonged rupture of membranes
I. History of type I diabetes mellitus
J. Prolonged labor lasting >16 hours
